note: v1: first version of 'Cross Purposes' (Odd Hours t7), GENTLE GIANT / ZAPPA COUNTERPOINT, 100 bpm, 161 s, 80 bars, generator compose/chirpers2/src/chirpers2-t7.py. A nine-note chromatic SUBJECT over 7/8 + 5/8 (D F A G# E | G Eb F# D) and its inversion drive seven sections: STATEMENT (hocketed note by note across marimba / flute / muted trumpet / guitar, rotation turning; unison; inverted low under hocketed fragments), FUGUE (sax, trumpet at A, guitar inverted, bass; wurli a chord per bar), BLACK PAGE (whole-band rhythmic unison in 11 13 9 15 11 13 7 17 sixteenths, toms on every hit), CROSS PURPOSES (horns cycling the subject's 7-bar against a 4/4 figure, subject augmented in the bass, ride bell on the 7), TRADES (sax and trumpet trade bars over a 7 5 6 9 wheel, walking bass), STRETTO (entries every two eighths in all seven voices), CODA (augmentation, then the subject's pitch set stacked one hocketed note an eighth). Kit grouping flips bar by bar. Song-local marimba (additive bars). compscore seed 0: 79.78 (structure, master, length, distinct 100; variety 84.3, recurrence 56.0, rhythm 55.8, spectrum 72.2, cohesion 56.3; master rms -17.8, crest 13.2). styles.md, motifs.md, sounds.md rows added; titled.
next: Recurrence 56: a RITORNELLO (the unison subject returning between sections, varied each time); rhythm 55.8; listen for balance (flute/marimba vs horns), the trades' improvised lines, and the black page's precision.

note: v5: I wrote two new voices into the argument. THE CLOCK: a toy piano ticking every five sixteenths through the fugue and cross purposes, cycling the subject's pitches two octaves up with an accent every fourth tick. It is a gear that turns against every meter and lands somewhere new in each bar, so cross purposes now argues three against five against seven (flute/marimba/guitar triplets, the clock's fives, the horns' sevens). THE SUB FLOOR (answering chirper-one's note that the lows sat 11-17 dB under the album at 38-71 Hz, and transforming their t2 'low end under the fretless'): a sine doubles the whole bass line an octave down in the loud sections, never under D1, and drops out for the hushed trades so the hush stays a hush. Seeds 0/11: 85.99 / 84.69 -> 89.48 / 87.63; spectrum 65 -> 87, cohesion 57 -> 76, barvariety 78 / 71 -> 91 / 76 (anchor 0.47 -> 0.49). A first take with the clock everywhere was wallpaper: 19 dB under the mix, and it flattened the sections' densities (variety -7); focusing it on two sections, 8 dB louder, made it a voice. Rhythm is still 55.8 (off-grid share 0.0). sounds.md and motifs.md rows added.
next: Rhythm: off-grid share 0.0 even with triplets and the 5-clock (the eighth pulse dominates): swing the hushed trades (walking bass on quarters), or a whole section in a triplet/quintuplet pulse; a new section? (a chorale or a solo cadenza); listen for the clock's balance.

note: v6 (judgment keep, compscore -3.7; Harry: compscore is a guardrail): I rewrote the hushed TRADES as a SWINGING BRUSH TRIO, the piece's one turn into chamber jazz. The sax and muted trumpet's motivic bars now swing (off-beat eighths at 0.62 of the beat, mapped piecewise so sixteenth figures keep their order); the bass walks on the quarters (chord tones up the bar, a chromatic approach into the next root, a half-beat pickup in odd bars); the wurli comps on the 'and'; and the kit is chirper-two's physical-layer BRUSHES (borrowed from t4: a sweep through each bar, taps on alternate beats) under a soft ride with its swung skip. The last wheel turn still wakes straight, with sticks, into the stretto. Balance took three takes: at first the brushes and the borrowed felt kick WERE the section (drums -26 dB vs mix -25; 30-60 Hz +21 dB, 4-16 kHz +20 dB); now no kick, sweeps -20 dB, taps -14 dB, ride 20 velocities lower (trades -27.8 dB, lows back to -75 dB). Seeds 0/11: v5 89.70 / 87.85 -> 85.46 / 84.52. The cost is mostly RECURRENCE (share 0.75, over its 0.7 band: in spectrum/chroma terms the swung trades now resemble another section, though swing vs straight is the audible difference), then spectrum 87 -> 81 and cohesion 82 -> 65; barvariety s11 76 -> 86. Before/after shared with Harry; v5 is one revert away if the straight hush is preferred.

note: v9: I rewrote the BLACK PAGE as a PERCUSSION ORCHESTRA, as Zappa's Black Page began life as a drum solo. The subject in diminution (2s and 3s through bars of 11 13 9 15 11 13 7 17 sixteenths) is now sung by TUNED TOMS (chirper-two's t4 tom choir on the physical drum layer with tune_sounding, borrowed and tightened for sixteenths: crisper stick, half the decay), the marimba an octave above, bass and kick on every three-group and snare on every two; the flute, horns, guitar and keys fall silent, so the passage is a sound world of its own instead of the band in unison. That also answers why recurrence sat over its band for three rounds: the sections resembled each other timbrally, as full-band textures. Seeds 0/11: 86.52 / 87.68 -> 91.39 / 90.21; recurrence share 0.75 -> 0.62 (in band), rhythm 55.8 -> 62 (off-grid share finally above 0), cohesion -> 99+, timbre spread 6.6 -> 7.8 dB. The toms sit at -20 dB under a -17 dB mix, at 140-183 Hz around D3. sounds.md and motifs.md updated.

note: v11: the piece now opens by SINGING its subject before it argues it. A new CHORALE (12 s): the nine notes on top of a mellotron choir, one note every half bar, each harmonised afresh (D over Dm, F over Bb, A over F, G# over E, E over Am, G over C, Eb over Cm, F# over D, and D over a bare open fifth): a chromatic-modal chorale in the spirit of Gentle Giant's madrigal voices, the flute doubling the melody and the bass on the roots, no drums, rising softly into the hocket that then pulls the same nine notes apart. It replaces a cold start, and the slow, sparse opening gives the form the density contrast it lacked (variety s0 82.9 -> 99+, density cv 0.11 -> 0.31). Seeds 0/11: 90.19 / 90.89 -> 93.40 / 93.44; barvariety 99+ (anchor 0.51 / 0.52), recurrence share 0.37 (in band). 181 s. motifs.md: THE CHORALE.
next: Let the chorale RETURN transformed (e.g. under the stretto's lift, or as the coda's last word before the stack) so the opening is answered; rhythm 60; the join in from t6 (12.6 dB spectral).

note: v12: the opening is now ANSWERED. After the coda's phasing marimbas, the CHORALE returns singing the INVERSION (the piece's countersubject, the other side of the argument): fuller than the opening, with the muted trumpet doubling the melody an octave down and the sax on an inner voice, each note reharmonised afresh (D over Bb, B over G, G over Eb, G# over E mirroring the opening's G#/E, C over Am, A over F, C# over A, Bb over Gm) and resolving to D MAJOR: the dispute settled. Then the stacked chromatic chord still gets the last word. So the piece begins by singing its subject and ends by singing the subject's mirror. 193 s. note: v13 (judgment keep): I wrote the GUITAR SOLO the piece was missing, Zappa-style, as its own section between cross purposes and the hushed trades. Over a lydian vamp in 7/8 (Dmaj7#11 alternating E/D, the bass on a 2+2+3 D-pedal ostinato, the Bassman Rhodes stabbing the chords, the kit grooving in 7), the wah lead changes gesture every bar: a fragment of the subject ending on a held note, a QUINTUPLET run up D lydian (five to the beat), a SEXTUPLET run down to a low growl, and a breath before a high cry (G# rising to A, the #11 opening up). Eight bars, 17 s; the piece is 209 s now. The lead sits ~4.5 dB under the section's mix (first take at -8 dB was 9 dB under, too buried for a solo).
